educationalGoal: In Japanese Seminar, students receive an introduction to Japanese culture through lectures and hands-on experiences. Students will attend lectures given by experts in various topics related to Japanese culture and deepen their understanding through group discussions, reflection activities, and group projects. Students will conduct field research on a topic related to Japanese culture and share their findings with other students in the class.
advice: This course consists of 1) acquiring knowledge through pre-class readings and in-class lectures; 2) deepening and personalizing this knowledge through in-class discussions and reflection assignments; and 3) consolidating and synthesizing what they have learned through real-world observations and field work, culminating in a group presentation to share what they have learned. Japanese culture topics include: everyday life of a college student in Japan, daily activities, special occasions (festivals, special holidays, etc.), working in Japan, Kanazawa architecture, and religion in Japan. Course work consists of in-class activities and independent inquiry activities.

activityGoals.body: Understand their role in a group and work collaboratively.
Experience Japanese culture and participate in discussions about experiences in Japan.
Present research and field work results in a concise group presentation.
